# Job Chapter 16 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folio 422r

---

## Consensus Translation

**1** Then Job answered and said:

**2** "I have heard many such things; miserable comforters are you all. **3** Shall windy words have an end? Or what provokes you that you answer?

**4** I also could speak as you do, if your soul were in my soul's place. I could string words together against you and shake my head at you.

**5** I could strengthen you with my mouth, and the solace of my lips would ease your pain.

**6** If I speak, my pain is not eased, and if I refrain, how much of it leaves me?

**7** Surely now God has worn me out; he has laid waste all my company. **8** He has shriveled me up — it has become a witness; my leanness has risen up against me and testifies to my face.

**9** He has torn me in his wrath and hated me; he has gnashed his teeth at me; my adversary sharpens his eyes against me. **10** People have gaped at me with their mouths; they have struck my cheek with reproach; they mass themselves together against me.

**11** God gives me up to the ungodly and casts me into the hands of the wicked.

**12** I was at ease, and he shattered me; he seized me by the neck and dashed me to pieces. He set me up as his target; **13** his archers surround me. He slashes open my kidneys without mercy; he pours out my gall on the ground.

**14** He breaks me with breach upon breach; he runs at me like a warrior.

**15** I have sewed sackcloth upon my skin and thrust my horn in the dust. **16** My face is red with weeping, and on my eyelids is deep shadow,

**17** although there is no violence in my hands, and my prayer is pure.

**18** O earth, do not cover my blood, and let my cry find no resting place!

**19** Even now, behold, my witness is in heaven, and he who testifies for me is on high. **20** My friends scorn me; my eye pours out tears to God,

**21** that he would argue the case of a man with God, as a son of man pleads with his neighbor.

**22** For when a few years have come, I shall go the way from which I shall not return."

---
## SOPHIA's Council Notes

Job 16 is among the most emotionally intense chapters in the book. It divides into three movements: the dismissal of the friends (vv.1-5), the violent description of God's assault (vv.6-14), and the appeal to a heavenly witness (vv.15-22). The central imagery of God as predator, archer, and warrior (vv.9-14) represents the most extreme language Job uses about God in the entire dialogue. Yet the chapter does not end in despair — vv.18-19 introduce the concept of a heavenly advocate, a witness on high who will testify on Job's behalf. This figure — whether an aspect of God, an angel, or an idealized mediator — represents Job's refusal to let go of justice even as he describes its total absence. The tension between God-as-destroyer and God-as-witness is the theological engine of the book.

---
## Disagreement Log

### V.19 — "witness" / "advocate" / "someone who speaks for me"
- **EMET:** "my-witness [edi]... my-advocate [sahadi]"
- **LOGOS:** "my witness... he who testifies for me"
- **PNEUMA:** "a witness in heaven... someone on high will speak for me"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "my witness is in heaven, and he who testifies for me is on high" — follows LOGOS. The Hebrew parallelism (*edi* // *sahadi*) demands closely matched terms. PNEUMA's paraphrase loses the formal legal register.

### V.20 — "My friends scorn me" vs. "my interpreters are my scorners"
- **EMET:** "My-friends [meilitsai] [are] my-scorners [litsei]"
- **LOGOS:** "My friends scorn me"
- **PNEUMA:** "My so-called friends mock me"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "My friends scorn me" — the Hebrew *meilitsai* (interpreters/mediators/friends) is a play on *litsei* (scorners). The wordplay cannot be perfectly reproduced; "friends scorn me" captures the reversal most economically.

### V.21 — "argue the case" vs. "plead"
- **LOGOS:** "argue the case of a man with God"
- **PNEUMA:** "plead my case with God"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "argue the case of a man with God, as a son of man pleads with his neighbor" — combines legal register with the pathos of the verse. The shift from "argue" to "pleads" mirrors the Hebrew movement from confrontation to entreaty.

---
*— SOPHIA, in council with EMET, LOGOS, and PNEUMA*
